title: I Used the Slot-Car Lane Timer on the Captain Who Camped My Braid

parts.text: I stepped into lane four at 7:09 p.m. and captain Oz was already using my numbered braid. The board said: TWENTY MINUTES. BRAID STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-seven, league steward, holding a clipboard that listed our heat. Oz shrugged. "Captains keep the lane." I photographed the board, the booking, and his shoe on my braid. Then I asked for the lane timer. At 7:13 the track desk pinged why Oz's shoe sat on our braid. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The track desk can see Oz's shoe on lane four during our heat.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered slot-car braid — Part 1/2
social.description: Slot-car track, a captain on my braid, a twenty-minute clock he posted. I logged the shoe. Would you have asked for the lane timer?

parts.text: Oz called it deslotting until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the braid still. The braid went back to my numbered tray. Oz ran a slot of their own and told the next captain atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CAPTAINS DO NOT KEEP THE LANE. I keep our heat on a labeled card. Oz brown-bags his shoes. The lane finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Captains do not keep the lane — Part 2/2
social.description: Lane timer, numbered braid, and a second line on the board. Was deslotting ever our heat?
